COVER STORY

Double kicks. Dirty tackles. One ball.

Street Cup Brawlers takes the side-scrolling street brawler of the late NES era and smashes it into the five-a-side chaos of an arcade soccer game. Punch, kick and jump-kick your way through eleven stages, then turn the ball itself into a weapon.

The whole game is one HTML file. It draws to a tiny 426×240 canvas at 60 frames a second, scales up crisp, and runs on a desktop, on a phone with touch buttons coloured like a Super Nintendo pad, or with two real USB SNES controllers for couch co-op.

Every level ends in a roguelike reward: your score and time, then three upgrade cards that spin up like a fruit machine. Golden cards are legendary.

THE LORE

The summer of '89, as told by Dad

Story mode is a bedtime story that keeps getting less believable. Dad tells his kids how he won the streets back from Captain Chaos and his hooligans. Every stage is one of his tall tales; every cut-scene ends with a kid calling him out. By the last stage the room itself is coming apart.
